about.title: About me
about.summary: I originally come from the trades: After my apprenticeship in water supply, I took two sabbatical years from 2016 to 2018 to travel the world, teach myself Spanish, and work various jobs. Then I went to Berlin to HMP Heidenhain Microprint – a circuit board manufacturer – where, together with an external team, I converted an old control system into a computer-operated, fully automatic PLC control. That's when I discovered my passion for programming and moved to Robert Bosch GmbH in Nuremberg to complete an apprenticeship as an IT specialist for application development – shortened to 2.5 years and completed with distinction, just like my first apprenticeship. I built up the previously almost non-existent web development structure at the site practically single-handedly and got the first full-time developer position at the industrial manufacturing site NuP1. There I develop complex business web applications with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Prisma ORM – some used Bosch-wide or even worldwide.

Responsible for the entire product lifecycle – from requirements analysis to deployment.

bosch.title: Full-Stack Developer & Solution Architect
bosch.description: Managing multiple Red Hat Linux terminal servers (NGINX, PM2) as well as MSSQL database servers. Administering a GitHub Enterprise Server with over 126 repositories and 30+ users. Developing complex web applications with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Prisma ORM – some used Bosch-wide or worldwide. Many smaller scripts and applications that save employees a lot of time. Migrated legacy C# Blazor projects to modern JavaScript frameworks and created a site-wide web template with Bosch corporate design.

hmp.title: Water Treatment/Plant Operator + Electronics & Control Engineering
hmp.description: Plant operator of a water treatment facility until modernization of the plant control. Work on old controls and manual switch cabinets. Served as on-site contact for an external company to modernize the plant control. Together, the system was converted over two years into a computer-controlled, fully automatic PLC system. This was my first exposure to programming and sparked my desire to reorient toward becoming a programmer.
